analysis:
The PR threads one boolean, `buildsAhead`, from `QwenTensorParallelBatchSettings.resolve` (`batch.buildsAhead`) into a new stored property `batchBuildsAhead` in `QwenTensorParallelResidentRuntime.swift`. It is set at the call site near head line 398 and in the private init near head lines 434 and 445. `+Batch.swift` lines 232 and 234 pass it to both `QwenTensorParallelNativeBatchExecutor` and `QwenTensorParallelBatchDriver`. No authorization, attestation, encryption, key handling or prefix-cache scope/TTL logic changes. The sealed codec, data-plane agreement, load-agreement digest, per-request fingerprint check across ranks (`prepareBatch`), prefix scope derivation and memory gating are all untouched.

The comment says the value is the load agreement's own, so both ranks use one value. In the base `load()`, `batch.agreementFields` is already part of the load agreement hash. I could not see the settings source, so I cannot confirm that `buildsAhead` is included in `agreementFields`. If it is not, the ranks could diverge. That would be a rank-divergence or availability risk (TB-002, A-018), not a confidentiality risk, because collectives are sealed and authenticated and a mismatch would fail rather than leak. The driver and executor implementations of build-ahead are also unseen. They could affect lane/KV lifecycle, T-028 residual GPU data, or the cancellation semantics in T-010. Next-pass questions: confirm `buildsAhead` is in `batch.agreementFields`, and confirm build-ahead steps are drained or discarded on cancel, retire and failure without retaining history, since `serveBatch` still asserts `batchHost.isDrained`. No concrete regression is demonstrable from the supplied evidence.
